question.stimulus: Sid: The sign says “Keep off the grass.” Micki: I know, but just one person walking across the grass doesn’t hurt it. Sid: Your statement is false. If everyone believed as you do, everyone would walk across the grass, and the grass would die.
question.questionStem: Sid’s argument is questionable in that it

answerChoices.A: attempts to use a statement about the consequences of actions to disprove a statement about the actions themselves
answerChoices.B: treats a statement about the consequences of an action as though it were instead about the consequences of everyone believing the statement
answerChoices.C: contradicts itself by treating a statement that the arguer does not believe as though it were a statement believed by everyone
answerChoices.D: discounts the fact that there may be circumstances under which hurting the grass is justified
answerChoices.E: attempts to undermine a statement by calling into question the character of the person making the statement

question.stimulus: Science writer: Lemaître argued that the universe began with the explosion of a “primeval atom,” a singular point of infinite gravity in space and time. If this is correct, our current observations should reveal galaxies accelerating away from one another. This is precisely what we observe. Yet because there is another theory—the oscillating universe theory—that makes exactly this same prediction, Lemaître’s theory must be considered inadequate.
question.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a flaw in the science writer’s reasoning?

answerChoices.A: The conclusion is derived partly from assertions attributed to a purported expert whose credibility is not established.
answerChoices.B: The conclusion is based on a shift in meaning of a key term from one part of the argument to another part.
answerChoices.C: The science writer takes for granted the existence of a causal connection between observed phenomena.
answerChoices.D: The science writer fails to see that one theory’s correctly predicting observed data cannot itself constitute evidence against an alternative theory that also does this.
answerChoices.E: The science writer presumes, without providing justification, that there are only two possible explanations for the phenomena in question.

question.stimulus:
Dr. Khan: Professor Burns recognizes that recent
observations fail to confirm earlier ones that
apparently showed a comet reservoir far out in
our solar system. She claims this nonconfirmation
is enough to show that the earlier observations
are incorrect. But the recent observations
occurred under poor conditions.
question.questionStem:
Which one of the following is most supported by Dr.
Khan’s statements?

answerChoices.A: If the recent observations had been made under good conditions, they would have provided conclusive evidence of a comet reservoir far out in our solar system.
answerChoices.B: Contrary to Professor Burns’s view, the recent observations confirm the earlier ones.
answerChoices.C: Professor Burns’s claim about the implications of the recent observations is incorrect.
answerChoices.D: The recent observations, even if they had been made under good conditions, would not have been enough to suggest that the earlier ones are incorrect.
answerChoices.E: The poor conditions present during recent observations render them worthless.

question.stimulus:
Among Trinidadian guppies, males with large spots are
more attractive to females than are males with small
spots, who consequently are presented with less frequent
mating opportunities. Yet guppies with small spots are
more likely to avoid detection by predators, so in waters
where predators are abundant only guppies with small
spots live to maturity.
question.questionStem:
The situation described above most closely conforms to
which one of the following generalizations?

answerChoices.A: A trait that helps attract mates is sometimes more dangerous to one sex than to another.
answerChoices.B: Those organisms that are most attractive to the opposite sex have the greatest number of offspring.
answerChoices.C: Those organisms that survive the longest have the greatest number of offspring.
answerChoices.D: Whether a trait is harmful to the organisms of a species can depend on which sex possesses it.
answerChoices.E: A trait that is helpful to procreation can also hinder it in certain environments.

question.stimulus: In an experiment, researchers played a series of musical intervals—two-note sequences—to a large, diverse group of six-month-old babies. They found that the babies paid significantly more attention when the intervals were perfect octaves, fifths, or fourths than otherwise. These intervals are prevalent in the musical systems of most cultures around the world. Thus, humans probably have a biological predisposition to pay more attention to those intervals than to others.
question.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Several similar experiments using older children and adults found that these subjects, too, had a general tendency to pay more attention to octaves, fifths, and fourths than to other musical intervals.
answerChoices.B: None of the babies in the experiment had previous exposure to music from any culture.
answerChoices.C: All of the babies in the experiment had been exposed to music drawn equally from a wide variety of cultures around the world.
answerChoices.D: In a second experiment, these same babies showed no clear tendency to notice primary colors more than other colors.
answerChoices.E: Octaves, fifths, and fourths were played more frequently during the experiment than other musical intervals were.
